result:
Review of version 3, made from the texts alone; the three data files and my earlier passes were not in front of me, so item 2 leans on the drafter's account in section (6).

## 1. Blockers

**1.1 — P2, P10 and run 6 cover run O, where they are false or unargued.**
- Defect: under FLOOR0 and ONE-FEWER a birth can receive nothing, so S2 does not apply. The owner's arm B1 already shows both start knots failing the knot test in run O, and start knots are not joins.
- Fix, P2: "Under not-all-equal, in every run and history under the nine base laws (run O apart, where S2's hypothesis fails; its tie classes are reported), no tie class contains a made distinction; and the 60 third-pattern starts …"
- Fix, P10: begin "In runs 1 to 5: …" and end "Run O's knots are PO2's."
- Fix, run 6's row: "every not-all-equal run of runs 1 to 5".

**1.2 — Condition 2 in form has no round (D 5.1, claim 4).**
- Defect: "fewer than two of Y′" is undecidable without saying at which round.
- Fix: "run A with Y has, after every round read, fewer than two parts the same as Y′ (any descent) for every other member Y′ of the class, and the run with Y′ has two of Y′ made by X at some round read."

**1.3 — "A copier for some members of the class and not all" is undefined (POA; owner's arm A; claim 6).**
- Defect: condition 2's second half fails by construction for a partial copier, and nothing excludes X's own course. If one of the STEPS-1 made-4 cases survived renaming, it would be reported as "the outcome his sentence describes".
- Fix, add to the owner's arm A (i): "X is a copier for a member Y when, under the claim's law and one stated rule, run A with Y has two of Y made by X, surviving every renaming registered for the design, condition 3 holds, and (form) the run with each other member Y′ in Y's stead has fewer than two parts the same as Y after every round read. 'Some and not all': this holds for at least one member and not for every member, the same X, law and rule."

**1.4 — B3's sentence is not true by definition (P, "Settled" item 10; owner's arm B3).**
- Defect: condition 2 for Y says nothing about parts the same as Y in the run with Y′, and "two of Y′" there carries no descent.
- Fix: "…then the counts of parts the same as Y′ differ between the replacement runs with Y and with Y′, at the round at which the run with Y′ has two (fewer than two against at least two), so the parts by descent (D 5.3) differ. True by definition, when both runs reached that round."
- P16 stands as worded.

**1.5 — The step-2 sentence is wrong as stated (P, "Settled" item 6; survey, top).**
- Defect: with at most two holders a value can be tied at two loose places if they are the structure's only loose distinctions. Example: A{f1,a,b}, C{a,b,v}, B{v,c,d}, D{c,d,f2}; every knot passes and f1 = v = f2.
- Fix: "…so two usable loose places for one value, in a connected structure that keeps any other loose distinction (usable or barred), need a distinction with a third holder; …"

**1.6 — P6 predicts "every design", but made-2-exchanged was never read for values.**
- Defect: the first test had 11 designs; made-2-exchanged was added for the arm only, so the (a) mark is unearned for it.
- Fix: "Values, stated rules, made-2 to made-6 and the six designs with Y present from round 0: exactly one … (made-2-exchanged: reported.)"

**1.7 — "Survives n1 to n4" cannot be decided on the made designs (D 4.5; C and CF).**
- Defect: n2 is defined only for designs with Y present from round 0.
- Fix: "A case holds **under a stated rule** only if it survives every renaming registered for its design (n1, n3, n4 on the made designs; n1 to n4 on the others)."

**1.8 — Reading (iv) has no T and no round for (a) to (c) (D 7.8, D 7.1).**
- Fix, D 7.1: "T: the last round reached by every run the reading names (for (iii) also X alone and Y alone; for (iv) the run with Z and the run with Z barred)."
- Fix, D 7.8: "(a) with Z there, no two of Y after any round read; (b) with Z barred, two of Y after some round read; (c) with Z there, no two of Z after any round read; (d) Z makes a birth in round T of the run with Z."

**1.9 — Run 3 "as run 2" asks for runs that are not defined there.**
- Defect: X alone, Y alone and the renamings are defined only per design.
- Fix, run 3's readings: "as run 2 without the replacement runs, X alone, Y alone and reading (iii); in run 5 its cases are swapped under n1 and n4 only (n4 drawn with the pair start's name), unless starts.json lists more."

**1.10 — Run G's drawn check is underspecified.**
- Defect: neither the draw procedure nor the law of the "one round" is given.
- Fix: "The draw's procedure is the engine's own, recorded with its seed in the result note (P0 needs agreement, not these 600); the one round is under (FLOOR1, CANCEL-OFFSHOOT, RELEASE) with MET(OLDEST), parity."

**1.11 — The owner's arm C contradicts itself on the guard.**
- Defect: the intro says "none stopped by the guard", while C.2 and PO5 say run A of the made-4 case stops at the guard at round 6.
- Fix, intro: "1,728 runs; T is less than 6 where a run of the reading stopped at the bound of 500 knots or at the fold engine's guard: T = 6 in 1,606, …"

**1.12 — P3's "after round 2" is ambiguous.**
- Defect: STEPS-2's round-2 parts are in the roster after round 2.
- Fix: "no part the same as the two-knot part in the roster after any round t ≥ 3".

**1.13 — The census does not state its knot law.**
- Defect: 192 and 240 are 48 runs per design, so the counts are for one knot law or pooled, and the text does not say which.
- Fix: add "(under parity)" or "(runs counted once for both knot laws)", whichever the prototype did.

## 2. The ten required changes

Taken in the order of section (6), "A2 section 8".

1. Arm's runs and listings registered: done (residue 1.11).
2. POA: done, except that the partial copier is undefined (1.3) and (iv) lacks T and rounds (1.8).
3. B1 (c), (d) and the sentence in the claim and P: done.
4. Values condition 2, base-law quantifier, form class by family, made-4 wording: done, except that the form condition has no round (1.2) and n2 is undefined on made designs (1.7).
5. B3 and P16: P16 done; the B3 sentence in P item 10 and the owner's arm B3 is not done (1.4).
6. Implementer items: done as far as the texts show, except run G (1.10) and run 3 (1.9).
7. Marks: done.
8. Three-holder starts: done, but P2's scope now wrongly takes in run O (1.1).
9. Step-2 sentence: not done correctly (1.5).
10. Words: done, with the residues in item 6 below.

## 3. The three disagreements

The drafter is right on all three.

- **Condition 2 in values.** X alone has no place of Y and adds nothing. I would say it more plainly still: "In values the first half holds by construction and the second half is condition 1 for Y′, so condition 2 adds nothing in values; X alone is reported."
- **"Makes a birth in the last round read" with "has not ended".** The condition is needed, because an implied last birth leaves no member. Keep it.
- **Two of the three.** PO5's own list gives the count: two-22 under one law and both knot laws. Add "under one law, under both knot laws".

## 4. The plain sentences

Reading (i) in two parts is honest once 1.3 is applied. Readings (ii) to (iv) are honestly kept from being called support. I would change these sentences in the owner's arm, section D:

- **As seen.** Three faults: the made-4 form case survives n4, so "once the start is renumbered" overstates; "when" names a cause; and the made-4 case of (ii) exists only because T was cut to 5. Replacement:
  > "We have no copier yet, so there is nothing yet for what you called 'over-write' or 'break out' to act on. No fixed rule leaves two of every pattern in the class; where two of one pattern appear, they are gone under some renumbering of the start, or the first pattern makes them with nothing to meet. Under these laws no place of a pattern, and no relation among its distinctions, is changed by another; only its course changes. In three runs the first pattern has ended while the second still makes births, and had not ended by the same round with the second barred. One of the three counts only because that run was cut off at round 5: with the second barred the first pattern ends two rounds later than with the second there. The other two are one start of two patterns of the same kind, under one law and both knot laws. The reverse is seen in nine. A relation among one pattern's distinctions changed by the other's births was seen only under rations we do not use, and there the knot test fails."
- **A copier for some and not all.** "Your inkling" claims too much; only the first sentence is met. Replacement:
  > "This is the outcome the first sentence of your inkling describes: a copier for these patterns and not for those. Here is the smallest pattern it fails on and what that pattern does to the copier's course. Whether that is what your second sentence means, the runs do not say."
- **No case of (ii).** "Ends the other" names a cause. Replacement:
  > "In no run had the first pattern ended, with the second still making births, where it had not ended with the second barred."
- **Reading (iii).** It reads as a universal, and under MET the "X alone" clause is always met. Replacement:
  > "In 70 runs, 66 of them with a second pattern of more members and offshoots, the first pattern's course differs with whether the second is there and the second's does not differ with the first; in 8 runs it is the other way. Under MET the comparison with the first pattern alone always differs, so it adds nothing there."
- **Reading (iv).** "Named after, the two go to a place of the third" is true only with Z barred. Replacement:
  > "With a third pattern named before the second, the one case is gone, and it is there again when the third is barred. Named after the second, the case is gone too, and with the third barred the two are tied to a place of the third, not of the second. This goes with the names, as the case itself does. Under a fixed list of takes the third pattern removes nothing where the list still applies."

"A copier for the whole class" is fine as written.

## 5. Honesty of the stop

Yes in P: "neither a copier nor a reason there cannot be one", the F1 control, and "open" are all stated. Two additions would stop a reader of the claim alone from taking it for a negative result:

- Claim section 5, after "All of these are predicted to fail": "A failure of every C(r, b) is about one first pattern, four stated rules and the registered classes; it is no reason that no made pattern can, and for values under parity the question stays undecided (P, 'What a result would and would not show')."
- P, the expected-result bullet, on F1: after "in every design under some history" add "(seen under COPY-LAW(CANCEL-OFFSHOOT) only)".

## 6. Words

- "the question under parity is open" (P): the glossary's "open" has another sense. Use "is not decided".
- "at the same place among that parent's offshoots" (D 7.8): "place" is defined. Use "have the same number in the order of that parent's offshoots of the round".
- "in Y's place" (P disclosure; section 3's "in Y's stead" is mine): use "as the second pattern". "with X in place of Y" (D 4.3): use "with X for Y".
- "by position", "in both positions" (D 7.8, P "Starts and files"): use "by their order in the start's list" and "named before Y and named after Y".
- "the link e", "the barred link" (D, P, claim): a new noun. Use "the shared distinction e".
- "halves" (claim 1, D 1.4): use "two parts".
- "is stopped" for the second or third pattern (owner's arm D): SD's "stopped" means something else. Use "is barred".
- "over-write or break out of" outside his quotation, and "rewritten" / "Rewriting" (owner's arm B1 heading and D): use the wording in item 4 and "changed".
- "copying a form" and "can copy under parity" (claim 5, P): use "leaving two parts the same as a second pattern" and "can leave two of what it meets under parity".
- "the form below" (P, "Settled"): use "the form given here".
- "cuts met sets down", "cut-down piece" (P item 10, owner's arm B3): use "restricts each met set to" and "the restricted remainder of a mixed part".
- "far away" (P, prior work): use the record's own wording for that result, or drop the phrase.
- "the larger" (owner's arm D, (iii)): use "of more members".

## 7. Verdict

**Freeze**, with the fixes of 1, 4, 5 and 6 applied by the thread. All are sentence-level; none needs a new run or changes a registered count.
